currentContext.strengths: Largest music IP library in India - 1,80,000+ songs across 14+ languages, plus 70+ films, 55+ digital series and over 10k+ hours of television serials|Very long-duration IP economics: new content is structured to pay back in approximately five years, fully amortise over roughly a decade, and continue earning at near-90% margins for 60-80 years thereafter|Owned distribution reach - YouTube channels generating 1,123 Bn+ views and 200 Mn+ subscribers|Monetisation diversified across six revenue streams, reducing dependence on any single distribution channel or vertical|Breadth of platform relationships - 50+ music licensing platforms, 30+ streaming platforms, 20+ broadcasting platforms and 8+ social media platforms|Agreement with Bhansali Productions secures premium Hindi film music on pre-agreed commercial terms, insulating the Company from competitive bidding|Artiste management roster of 300+ artistes with a combined digital footprint of 410 Mn+, enabling cross-monetisation across Music, Video and Live Events|Disciplined pre-licensing model in digital series - projects greenlit only after securing platform interest and approval|Proprietary analytics and AI-led production tooling that cut music-video production from over two weeks to a few days
currentContext.strategies: Build an integrated entertainment ecosystem - the Entertainment Flywheel - by reinforcing each vertical and the interconnections between them, rather than scaling individual businesses in isolation|Three cross-cutting accelerators run across the verticals: AI & Data Analytics, Brand Partnerships and Performance Marketing|Digital Tailwinds: leverage macro-expansion of internet users, higher per-user consumption and the migration of advertising budgets to digital platforms|Monetisation Catalysts: capture structural upside from acceleration of paid audio subscriptions and the potential for short-format digital applications to share advertising revenue|Market Share Expansion: sustain targeted new-content investment to capture and control 25% to 30% of all new music released in India|Financial Discipline: secure high-value IP and marketing efficiencies through the strategic stake in Bhansali Productions (predictable costs for Hindi film music) and Pocket Aces (in-house digital amplification)|Maintain a non-negotiable five-year payback requirement on all new music content acquired|Shift the Video vertical away from capital-heavy in-house film production toward risk-mitigated, IP-led, asset-light formats anchored by significant-minority ownership positions, while retaining ownership of underlying IP wherever feasible|Run Live Events on two legs - lean, artiste-led concerts using third-party venues with low working capital, and higher-margin owned-IP shows and festivals - under a test-and-scale operating philosophy|Reorient Carvaan retail toward profitability via e-commerce and modern trade, SKU rationalisation and organisational restructuring, while scaling vinyl|Refresh the legacy catalogue with licensed Generative AI tools through a dedicated AI efficiency team to make 20th-century content monetisable for Gen Z audiences|Expand internationally in live entertainment and events through the newly incorporated UAE subsidiary, and pursue selective strategic investments and acquisitions in the creator economy|Pursue entertainment opportunities on the strength of their IP potential, monetisation and returns rather than the stature of the opportunity alone
currentContext.expansion: Saregama is an asset-light, IP-led business: its expansion is content-portfolio and corporate-development led rather than plant-and-capacity led, and the AR discloses no manufacturing capacity. The core programme is the commitment to invest INR 10,000 Mn between FY 25 and FY 27 to expand the music IP portfolio, targeting 25-30% of all new Indian music content, with each acquisition governed by a five-year payback framework. During FY 26 the Company acquired NAV Records to build its position in the Haryanvi music ecosystem, and entered an agreement with Bhansali Productions securing premium Hindi film music on pre-agreed commercial terms - a structure the MD describes as taking a 28% to 49.9% stake funded entirely from internal accruals with an initial payment of INR 3,250 Mn. On the corporate-development side, the Company completed the second tranche acquisition in Pocket Aces Pictures Private Limited on 3rd April, 2025 by acquiring 4,111 securities, lifting fully diluted shareholding to 90.93%; Pocket Aces in turn acquired 100% of Finnet Media Private Limited on 19th November, 2025 (with a further 2,88,235 OCPS to be acquired after two years), extending the Group into influencer marketing and creator management. International footprint was extended by incorporating the wholly owned subsidiary Saregama Performing Arts & Music Festivals L.L.C S.O.C in Dubai Mainland, UAE - approved by the Board on 5th September, 2025 with the Commercial Licence issued on 20th February, 2026 - to build live entertainment and events across the Middle East and other global markets. Within the existing verticals, expansion is format-led: adjacent formats such as Carvaan, Vinyl and live experiences, a test-and-scale approach to new live formats including the inaugural proprietary two-day UN40 festival in Bengaluru in March 2026, and a deliberate scaling down of capital-heavy in-house film production in favour of risk-mitigated, IP-led formats with significant-minority ownership positions. Retail expansion runs the other way - Carvaan is being reoriented toward profitability through a shift to e-commerce and modern trade, SKU rationalisation and organisational restructuring, while vinyl volumes scaled from 4,000 units in FY 24 to 27,000 units in FY 26.
currentContext.mdna: Indian M&E sector expanded 9.1% to INR 2.78 Tn in 2025, outpacing nominal GDP per capita growth of 7.7%; digital media surpassed television to become the largest single segment, breaching the INR 1 Tn milestone|Global recorded music revenue grew 7% to USD 32 Bn in 2025 with streaming at 69% of revenue, while India remains among the most under-penetrated large music markets globally - a structural opportunity, not a constraint|India's paid music-subscription penetration of 3% versus 18-67% in comparable markets, with dual levers of subscriber expansion and rising ARPU (emerging-markets label-share ARPU of ~8 USD against ~31 USD in developed markets, a ~4x runway)|Music subscription penetration remains under 3% despite India housing 18% of the world's population; the transition toward subscription-led consumption is an important long-term opportunity as willingness to pay for premium content rises|Organised live events grew 44% in 2025 to INR 145 Bn, the fastest-growing M&E vertical, with concerts, ticketed events and IP-led properties driving growth; devotional events benefit from rising engagement in spiritual experiences and government support for pilgrimage and cultural tourism, and comedy is now a top contributor to ticketed revenue|Video entertainment scaled to a record INR 205 Bn in 2025 with theatrical up 14%, though secondary-window economics continued to rationalise; India's micro-drama market at INR 6.5 Bn is expected to grow over 50% annually through 2028 on Tier-II/Tier-III adoption, low-cost AI-enabled production and UPI AutoPay|Music IP is a resilient, long-duration asset class with recurring monetisation across audio and video streaming, social media, publishing, licensing, films, television, gaming, live entertainment, consumer products and AI-enabled platforms|Rising consumption of regional content and the global appeal of Indian music enhance the long-term value of high-quality IP portfolios|New content economics: pays back in approximately five years, fully amortises over roughly a decade, and continues earning at near-90% margins for 60-80 years thereafter|With Pocket Aces achieving breakeven during the year, the short-format and digital series business is expected to deliver healthy growth in the years ahead|Live Events focus is on differentiated formats, a capital-efficient model and improving profitability over time|The Bhansali Productions partnership secures marquee Hindi film music at predictable costs, insulating the Company from unpredictable competitive bidding wars|Exclusive, pre-agreed pipeline for marquee Hindi film music secured through the Bhansali Productions partnership, expected to represent approximately 30% to 40% of future Hindi film music acquisitions|Premium Hindi film music pipeline supporting the Music segment through the partnership with Bhansali Productions, on pre-agreed commercial terms|Digital series operate on a disciplined pre-licensing model - projects greenlit only after securing platform interest and approval; the FY 26 slate included Bakaiti (ZEE5), High Heels S2 (YouTube), Yeh Saali Naukri (YouTube) and Hunter 2 (Amazon MX Player)|Television is a stable, capital-efficient vertical generating recurring revenue through commissioned programming on long-standing broadcaster relationships|Licensing pre-licensing contracts used to secure upfront revenue|Management cites a strong content pipeline supporting the integrated operating model

risks.risk: Infringement of the Company's intellectual property / piracy
risks.note: The core business relies on monetising music, film and content rights, so unauthorised use or piracy directly impacts revenue, weakens the value of exclusive content and increases legal costs, while damaging credibility as a rights holder and making licensing harder to enforce. Flagged as a material issue with negative financial implications; mitigated by a dedicated monitoring team and membership of industry body IMI (Indian Music Industry).

risks.risk: Investment return risk on content and artiste spend
risks.note: Investments in content and artiste collaborations may not always deliver expected returns, affecting profitability and future growth. Mitigated by diversified, data-driven investments across music, films, digital content and events, a focus on low-risk high-return projects, retained IP ownership, and piloting initiatives before scaling.

Unfavourable licensing renewals or rates may reduce revenue streams. Mitigated by a large, high-quality content library with multiple platform deals to reduce dependence on any one counterparty, and pre-licensing contracts that secure upfront revenue.

risks.risk: Content cost inflation and competitive intensity
risks.note: Increased competition may drive up content costs or lower success rates, impacting overall performance. Mitigated through industry relationships, a diversified multilingual content strategy, predictive analytics and partnerships with established artistes.

risks.risk: Digital disruption and shifting consumption habits
risks.note: Rapid technology evolution and changing consumption habits may impact traditional revenues; digitalisation has already altered how music revenue is generated. The Company invests in digital innovation, new platforms and tech upgrades, and uses data analytics to drive content strategy - treating digitalisation as an opportunity as well as a risk.
Over-reliance on certain genres or platforms can limit reach and revenue. Mitigated by a broad portfolio spanning multiple languages, genres, formats and platforms.

Difficulty attracting and retaining talent can reduce operational efficiency in a business whose output depends on creative and monetisation expertise. Mitigated by a balanced scorecard for performance, employee stock options, decentralisation and regular engagement and training programmes.

risks.risk: Regulatory change, including environmental compliance in the products business
risks.note: Changes in regulations or IP infringement may harm business operations and financial outcomes; separately, the products business must comply with E-waste and Plastic waste regulations, where non-adherence to changing environmental legislation on generation, collection and disposal can create monetary risk. Mitigated by proactive legal monitoring, industry engagement, robust anti-piracy efforts and close collaboration with relevant authorities.

risks.risk: Macro-economic weakness and inflation compressing discretionary spend
risks.note: A weak macroeconomic environment combined with high inflation may reduce the disposable income of the target market for discretionary entertainment spend. Management's counter-argument is that rising per capita income, increasing digitisation and greater affordability position the Indian economy to drive M&E growth and subscriber penetration.

risks.risk: Funding availability for content and artiste development (finance risk)
risks.note: Limited cash or financing could restrict investment in content and artiste development. Mitigated by maintaining net debt-free status and strong operating cash flows to ensure sufficient liquidity.

one-line thesis: Saregama delivered record EBITDA and PAT driven by music vertical growth post-Airtel Wynk exit, with strategic content spend discipline and new monetization levers like UN40 festival and Bhansali partnership creating durable upside; the shift from vanity-driven acquisitions to 5-year payback discipline and AI efficiency gains positions it as India’s dominant music IP infrastructure play.
financial scorecard: revenue: +19% YoY to INR 287cr (Q4); EBITDA/margin: +31% YoY to INR 133cr, 46.3% margin (Q4); PAT (rptd): +37% YoY to INR 105cr; PAT (normalized): +37% YoY (no material one-offs; royalty provision reversals are cyclical and offset by prior-year over-provisioning); order book: N/A; net debt: Net cash position strengthened (no debt, INR 1,200cr+ cash reserves)
guidance: revenue growth: 20-23% CAGR for music vertical (licensing + artist mgmt + retail); margin: 60-65% EBITDA margin for music vertical; order inflow: N/A; capex/commissioning: FY27 content spend INR 300-350cr; UN40 festival to break even by FY28; Carvaan Live concerts scaling; Bhansali deal locks in A/B+ film music for 24-30 months
segment / subsidiary detail: Music vertical: INR 814cr revenue (+17% YoY), EBITDA INR 517cr (+22% YoY), net margin INR 377cr (+28% YoY); Live events: INR 62cr revenue (excl. FY25 one-off Diljit tour), UN40 festival loss in Q4 due to inaugural spend; Video: INR 108cr (-44% YoY) due to deliberate wind-down of Yoodlee film production; Artist management: 300+ artists, 400M+ digital followers; Retail (Carvaan): Stable, integrated with live events; Bhansali: Strategic minority stake, exclusive access to future film music via performance-linked valuation
growth verticals / optionality: Punjabi music market entry (new model: combined recorded + live deals); US diaspora tours (Ilaiyaraaja, Sudesh Bhosle); AI licensing partnerships (future monetization); UN40 festival expansion (annual); short-form video monetization via Pocket Aces
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expansion driven by: (1) removal of Wynk revenue from denominator; (2) higher mix of paid subscription revenue; (3) lower incremental marketing cost via Pocket Aces digital footprint; (4) amortization of prior-year hits (Stree 2, Amaran) benefiting FY26; (5) no new content over-investment in FY26 (INR 235cr vs planned) due to film delays
capex / expansion: FY27 content spend: INR 300-350cr; Capex for UN40 festival: one-time investment in FY26; Carvaan Live concerts: low capex; Bhansali investment: equity stake, not capex; AI efficiency team: minimal tech spend
capital allocation: Prioritize music content (70%+ of capex); reinvest in artist management & live events; maintain net cash position; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; future AI licensing deals to be opportunistic, not capex-heavy
risks & watch-items: Punjabi market execution risk; festival breakeven delayed beyond FY28; AI regulatory uncertainty; subscription growth slower than expected; content ROI misjudgment on new releases
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined, long-term oriented; emphatic on economic rigor (no vanity buys), proud of operational efficiency (Pocket Aces breakeven), bullish on India’s subscription runway, dismissive of AI-generated content threat, focused on institutionalizing IP as infrastructure
non-obvious takeaways: Pocket Aces’ digital muscle is now a cost-saving engine for music marketing, not just a content creator; UN40’s non-music elements (comedy, games) are strategic differentiators reducing artist dependency; Bhansali deal effectively locks in premium Hindi film music without upfront licensing fees; Saregama’s non-digital revenue (physical, radio, sync) remains #1 in India despite digital focus

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian M&E sector expanded 9.1% to INR 2.78 Tn in 2025, outpacing nominal GDP per capita growth of 7.7%; digital media surpassed television to become the largest single segment, breaching the INR 1 Tn milestone
- Global recorded music revenue grew 7% to USD 32 Bn in 2025 with streaming at 69% of revenue, while India remains among the most under-penetrated large music markets globally - a structural opportunity, not a constraint
- India's paid music-subscription penetration of 3% versus 18-67% in comparable markets, with dual levers of subscriber expansion and rising ARPU (emerging-markets label-share ARPU of ~8 USD against ~31 USD in developed markets, a ~4x runway)
- Music subscription penetration remains under 3% despite India housing 18% of the world's population; the transition toward subscription-led consumption is an important long-term opportunity as willingness to pay for premium content rises
- Organised live events grew 44% in 2025 to INR 145 Bn, the fastest-growing M&E vertical, with concerts, ticketed events and IP-led properties driving growth; devotional events benefit from rising engagement in spiritual experiences and government support for pilgrimage and cultural tourism, and comedy is now a top contributor to ticketed revenue
- Video entertainment scaled to a record INR 205 Bn in 2025 with theatrical up 14%, though secondary-window economics continued to rationalise; India's micro-drama market at INR 6.5 Bn is expected to grow over 50% annually through 2028 on Tier-II/Tier-III adoption, low-cost AI-enabled production and UPI AutoPay
- Music IP is a resilient, long-duration asset class with recurring monetisation across audio and video streaming, social media, publishing, licensing, films, television, gaming, live entertainment, consumer products and AI-enabled platforms
- Rising consumption of regional content and the global appeal of Indian music enhance the long-term value of high-quality IP portfolios
- New content economics: pays back in approximately five years, fully amortises over roughly a decade, and continues earning at near-90% margins for 60-80 years thereafter
- With Pocket Aces achieving breakeven during the year, the short-format and digital series business is expected to deliver healthy growth in the years ahead
- Live Events focus is on differentiated formats, a capital-efficient model and improving profitability over time
- The Bhansali Productions partnership secures marquee Hindi film music at predictable costs, insulating the Company from unpredictable competitive bidding wars
- Exclusive, pre-agreed pipeline for marquee Hindi film music secured through the Bhansali Productions partnership, expected to represent approximately 30% to 40% of future Hindi film music acquisitions
- Premium Hindi film music pipeline supporting the Music segment through the partnership with Bhansali Productions, on pre-agreed commercial terms
- Digital series operate on a disciplined pre-licensing model - projects greenlit only after securing platform interest and approval; the FY 26 slate included Bakaiti (ZEE5), High Heels S2 (YouTube), Yeh Saali Naukri (YouTube) and Hunter 2 (Amazon MX Player)
- Television is a stable, capital-efficient vertical generating recurring revenue through commissioned programming on long-standing broadcaster relationships
- Licensing pre-licensing contracts used to secure upfront revenue
- Management cites a strong content pipeline supporting the integrated operating model

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin expansion driven by: (1) removal of Wynk revenue from denominator; (2) higher mix of paid subscription revenue; (3) lower incremental marketing cost via Pocket Aces digital footprint; (4) amortization of prior-year hits (Stree 2, Amaran) benefiting FY26; (5) no new content over-investment in FY26 (INR 235cr vs planned) due to film delays

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritize music content (70%+ of capex); reinvest in artist management & live events; maintain net cash position; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; future AI licensing deals to be opportunistic, not capex-heavy

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Saregama is an asset-light, IP-led business: its expansion is content-portfolio and corporate-development led rather than plant-and-capacity led, and the AR discloses no manufacturing capacity. The core programme is the commitment to invest INR 10,000 Mn between FY 25 and FY 27 to expand the music IP portfolio, targeting 25-30% of all new Indian music content, with each acquisition governed by a five-year payback framework. During FY 26 the Company acquired NAV Records to build its position in the Haryanvi music ecosystem, and entered an agreement with Bhansali Productions securing premium Hindi film music on pre-agreed commercial terms - a structure the MD describes as taking a 28% to 49.9% stake funded entirely from internal accruals with an initial payment of INR 3,250 Mn. On the corporate-development side, the Company completed the second tranche acquisition in Pocket Aces Pictures Private Limited on 3rd April, 2025 by acquiring 4,111 securities, lifting fully diluted shareholding to 90.93%; Pocket Aces in turn acquired 100% of Finnet Media Private Limited on 19th November, 2025 (with a further 2,88,235 OCPS to be acquired after two years), extending the Group into influencer marketing and creator management. International footprint was extended by incorporating the wholly owned subsidiary Saregama Performing Arts & Music Festivals L.L.C S.O.C in Dubai Mainland, UAE - approved by the Board on 5th September, 2025 with the Commercial Licence issued on 20th February, 2026 - to build live entertainment and events across the Middle East and other global markets. Within the existing verticals, expansion is format-led: adjacent formats such as Carvaan, Vinyl and live experiences, a test-and-scale approach to new live formats including the inaugural proprietary two-day UN40 festival in Bengaluru in March 2026, and a deliberate scaling down of capital-heavy in-house film production in favour of risk-mitigated, IP-led formats with significant-minority ownership positions. Retail expansion runs the other way - Carvaan is being reoriented toward profitability through a shift to e-commerce and modern trade, SKU rationalisation and organisational restructuring, while vinyl volumes scaled from 4,000 units in FY 24 to 27,000 units in FY 26.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, disciplined, long-term oriented; emphatic on economic rigor (no vanity buys), proud of operational efficiency (Pocket Aces breakeven), bullish on India’s subscription runway, dismissive of AI-generated content threat, focused on institutionalizing IP as infrastructure

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Largest music IP library in India - 1,80,000+ songs across 14+ languages, plus 70+ films, 55+ digital series and over 10k+ hours of television serials
- Very long-duration IP economics: new content is structured to pay back in approximately five years, fully amortise over roughly a decade, and continue earning at near-90% margins for 60-80 years thereafter
- Owned distribution reach - YouTube channels generating 1,123 Bn+ views and 200 Mn+ subscribers
- Monetisation diversified across six revenue streams, reducing dependence on any single distribution channel or vertical
- Breadth of platform relationships - 50+ music licensing platforms, 30+ streaming platforms, 20+ broadcasting platforms and 8+ social media platforms
- Agreement with Bhansali Productions secures premium Hindi film music on pre-agreed commercial terms, insulating the Company from competitive bidding
- Artiste management roster of 300+ artistes with a combined digital footprint of 410 Mn+, enabling cross-monetisation across Music, Video and Live Events
- Disciplined pre-licensing model in digital series - projects greenlit only after securing platform interest and approval
- Proprietary analytics and AI-led production tooling that cut music-video production from over two weeks to a few days

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Punjabi market execution risk; festival breakeven delayed beyond FY28; AI regulatory uncertainty; subscription growth slower than expected; content ROI misjudgment on new releases

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Pocket Aces’ digital muscle is now a cost-saving engine for music marketing, not just a content creator; UN40’s non-music elements (comedy, games) are strategic differentiators reducing artist dependency; Bhansali deal effectively locks in premium Hindi film music without upfront licensing fees; Saregama’s non-digital revenue (physical, radio, sync) remains #1 in India despite digital focus

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Build an integrated entertainment ecosystem - the Entertainment Flywheel - by reinforcing each vertical and the interconnections between them, rather than scaling individual businesses in isolation
- Three cross-cutting accelerators run across the verticals: AI & Data Analytics, Brand Partnerships and Performance Marketing
- Digital Tailwinds: leverage macro-expansion of internet users, higher per-user consumption and the migration of advertising budgets to digital platforms
- Monetisation Catalysts: capture structural upside from acceleration of paid audio subscriptions and the potential for …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Group] Saregama is part of the RP-Sanjiv Goenka (RPSG) Group, whose businesses span power and energy, carbon black, retail, IT enabled services, FMCG, media and entertainment, and agriculture.
- [Demerger] FY23 numbers are re-stated, as applicable, post the impact of the demerger; the FY26 cash flow also shows INR 36 Mn 'Transferred pursuant to Demerger/ Finnet'.
- [Base effect] Live events is described as lumpy in nature, with FY25 carrying a one-off Diljit Dosanjh India tour - the reason FY26 headline revenue (INR 9,846 Mn) is below FY25 (INR 11,713 Mn) while the deck flags revenue up excluding the one-off live-events base.
- [Regulation] An exceptional item of INR (85) Mn in FY26 is attributed to the impact of the new labour code.
- [Non-GAAP] The disclaimer states EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA Margin, PAT Margin, Debt to Equity, and ROE are non-GAAP measures not defined under Ind AS and may not be comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies.
